  release("Server4", 1)
  ##Checkout
  seize("Server5",1)
  timeout(function() rnorm(1,5))
  release("Server5", 1)
  
  
  sim %>%
    add_resource(name = "Server1", 1) %>%
    add_resource(name = "Server2", 1) %>%
    add_resource(name = "Server3", 1) %>%
    add_resource(name = "Server4", 1) %>%
    add_resource(name = "Server5", 1) %>%
   add_generator("Customer", Customer, function() rnorm(1,10,2))
  
  sim %>% run(until=1000)
  
  sim %>% now()
  
  sim %>% peek(3)
  
  
  Can someone please advise?

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: no applicable method for 'seize' applied to an object of class "character"
parts:
Still a pipe missing in line release("Server3", 1), over "## Guac anc
cheese". That's why your editor is not producing a homogeneous
indentation. Try with this:

Customer <- trajectory("Customer In Line") %>%
set_attribute("start_time", function() {now(sim)}) %>%
## Burrito, bowl, or tacos
seize("Server1", 1) %>%
timeout(function() rnorm(1, 15)) %>%
release("Server1", 1) %>%
## Rice and meat
seize("Server2", 1) %>%
timeout(function() rnorm(1, 20)) %>%
release("Server2", 1) %>%
## Salad and salsa
seize("Server3", 1) %>%
timeout(function() rnorm(1, 5)) %>%

## Guac anc cheese
seize("Server4",1) %>%
timeout(function() rnorm(1,5)) %>%
release("Server4", 1) %>%
##Checkout
seize("Server5",1) %>%
timeout(function() rnorm(1,5)) %>%
release("Server5", 1) %>%
log_(function() {paste("Finished: ", now(sim))})

Long explanation follows. The pipe operator sets the left-hand side as
first argument of the right-hand side. Every simmer activity (see
?seize, for instance) has the following signature: activity(.trj,
...), which means that they need a trajectory as a first argument. In
other words, this

trajectory() %>%
seize("resource", 1) %>%
release("resource", 1)

is equivalent to this not so convenient version:

release(seize(trajectory(), "resource", 1), "resource", 1)

Therefore, if you miss a pipe (before seize in this case), you break
the chain, and at some point the first argument is not a trajectory
(it is the "Server3" string in this case), hence the error.
